title: Why Good Experience Can End Joint Activity
abstract: arXiv:2611.02292v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Learning a partner's preferences through joint activity can make both partners worse off than receiving no feedback from the activity. We study a responder who values the partner's payoff but bears a cost when joining is attributed to personal interest. Both partners observe noisy evidence of whether the responder wanted the activity, available only after participation. Evidence of interest raises this cost, discouraging joining on unwanted days; joining only on wanted days would then be too revealing to sustain. With choices based on current payoffs, we derive a condition under which learning can end participation without ever making stopping beneficial to either partner. Feedback accuracy and preference persistence described by couples' diaries satisfy this condition at baseline payoffs. Once activity stops, no further evidence arrives and the belief that the responder generally wants the activity stays fixed, so waiting may never rest

translated_title: 为什么美好的体验反而可能终结共同活动
translated_abstract: 通过共同活动了解伴侣的偏好，可能使双方的境况都比没有从活动中获得任何反馈时更糟。我们研究了一个响应者，他重视伴侣的收益，但当其参与被归因于个人兴趣时会承担成本。双方只能在实际参与之后，才能观察到关于响应者是否真心想要这项活动的含噪证据。表明“有兴趣”的证据会提高这一成本，从而抑制在不想要的日子里的参与；而只在想要的日子里参与，又会因暴露过多信息而难以持续。在基于当期收益做出选择的前提下，我们推导出了一个条件：在此条件下，学习过程可以终结参与，而停止却从未对任何一方有利。伴侣日记所刻画的反馈准确性和偏好持续性在基线收益水平下满足这一条件。一旦活动停止，就不再有新证据到来，关于响应者总体上想要这项活动的信念将保持固定，因此等待可能永远无法重新启动参与。
tldr: 本文揭示了一个反直觉机制：共同活动产生的“有兴趣”证据会提高被归因于个人兴趣的成本，使得偏好学习过程能够在双方都未从停止中获益的情况下自然终结参与，且真实伴侣日记数据满足这一理论条件。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that noisy evidence of interest gathered through joint activity raises the cost of being attributed personal interest, so learning can end participation even though stopping is never beneficial to either partner—and real couples' diary data satisfy the derived condition.
